parameters.name: numerator
parameters.description: The value to be divided. Can be a measure, column reference, or numeric expression.
parameters.examNote: Can be any expression returning a number. If the numerator is BLANK, DIVIDE returns BLANK regardless of the denominator.

parameters.name: denominator
parameters.description: The value to divide by. If this equals zero or is BLANK, the alternateResult is returned instead of raising an error.
parameters.examNote: DIVIDE protects against division by zero. Without DIVIDE, using the / operator on a zero denominator throws an error and breaks the visual.

parameters.name: alternateResult
parameters.description: The value returned when the denominator is zero or BLANK. Defaults to BLANK() if not specified.
parameters.examNote: Common choices are 0 (to show zero in visuals) or BLANK() (to hide the cell entirely). Choose based on whether a blank or zero is more meaningful for the business context.

returnType: Decimal (result of numerator / denominator), or alternateResult when denominator is zero or blank
summary: DIVIDE performs safe division by returning an alternate result instead of throwing a divide-by-zero error when the denominator is zero or blank. It is the recommended replacement for the / operator in any measure where the denominator may not always have a value. DIVIDE is especially important in ratios, percentages, and per-unit calculations that appear on report visuals where a single error cell can break the entire visual.

examples.label: Profit margin percentage
examples.explanation: For Bike: 300/1000 = 0.30. For Helmet: 50/200 = 0.25. For Lock: Revenue = 0 so DIVIDE returns the alternateResult 0 instead of an error.

examples.label: Risky division without DIVIDE
examples.explanation: When Revenue = 0, the / operator throws a division by zero error that shows as an error cell in the visual. DIVIDE(Profit, Revenue, 0) or DIVIDE(Profit, Revenue) would return 0 or BLANK instead.

commonTraps: Using the / operator instead of DIVIDE causes error cells when the denominator is zero. Always prefer DIVIDE in measures used on report visuals.
DIVIDE(a, b) and DIVIDE(a, b, 0) behave differently when b = 0. The first returns BLANK (cell is empty), the second returns 0 (cell shows zero). Choose based on visual intent.
If the numerator is BLANK, DIVIDE returns BLANK regardless of the denominator value — this is intentional behavior, not a bug.

sqlEquivalent.expression: CASE WHEN denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator END
sqlEquivalent.note: SQL requires an explicit CASE WHEN to handle division by zero. DIVIDE encapsulates this logic in a single function call, making DAX measures much more concise and readable.
